newsitem.title: ITALY: Deficit-gdp goal reachable in 1997 - Italy's Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Deficit-gdp goal reachable in 1997 - Italy's Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday that the target of a three percent ratio between deficit and gross domestic product (GDP) required to join a single European currency was "realistic and reachable" in 1997.
"We believe that the three percent goal is realistic and reachable and we are comforted by today's cabinet discussions," Prodi told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
"The government reaffirms its will to follow the progress of revenue and spending day by day to meet the objectives of the 1997 budget," he said.

Prodi's 1997 austerity budget was designed to trim 62.5 trillion lire ($37.6 billion) off this year's deficit in a bid to become a founder member of European economic and monetary union (EMU) at its planned start in 1999.

Prodi told a parliamentary question time this week that Italy already made the grade on key inflation, interest rate and foreign exchange criteria laid down for EMU membership and was well on the way to reaching the three percent deficit-GDP goal.
He said Italy was also making progress on the fifth EMU criterion, that of reducing its overall debt towards 60 percent of GDP. Italy's ratio is currently at more than 120 percent.
